types.title: Transcript types
types.intro: Types steer the AI through two prompts: the cleanup prompt decides how the transcript is edited, the output-format prompt how the PDF is built from it. Builtin types can be adapted or deleted too; transcripts without a type give plain, unformatted text.
types.name: Name
types.structureHint: Decides what the PDF export builds from and how it structures without AI: dialogue and script start from the segments with their speakers, everything else from the processed text.
types.keepSections: Do not split sections across pages
types.keepSectionsHint: In a compilation export a file's section starts on a new page when it no longer fits on the current one, translations included. Sections that do fit stay where they are.
types.verbatim: The export reproduces the text unchanged
types.verbatimHint: The PDF export structures the processed text and the translations by itself, without an AI step: every sentence reaches the PDF unchanged and in its original order, and no heading appears that the text does not carry. Without this option the AI may rebuild the text for the export according to the output-format prompt — which only a type needs that turns its material into something else at export time. The option speaks for the export alone: how the AI processing works is decided by the option below.
types.promptHintDocument: Instruction for the LLM on how transcripts of this type should be edited. It runs once over the whole recording and writes the processed document from it — what stands here decides what comes out.
types.promptHintChunks: Instruction for the LLM on how transcripts of this type should be edited. The processing cleans section by section and hands back every sentence — this prompt describes the material to it, it is not an order to rewrite the text.
types.condenseHint: The cleanup prompt is then the instruction, and it runs once over the whole recording: a new document is written from digests of all sections — one title, one list of decisions, instead of one per section. That is what a type needs that turns the recording into something else, such as minutes or a summary. Without this option the transcript is cleaned section by section: spelling, punctuation and filler words are corrected, every sentence comes back, and the cleanup prompt only tells the AI what kind of text it is looking at.
types.condense: The AI processing writes a document of its own
types.promptOutputHint: Instruction for the LLM on how the processed text is split into blocks for the PDF export. Leaving it empty means the default prompt applies — it then shows as the field's placeholder. The cleanup prompt is added as context.
types.promptOutputUnused: Currently unused: while “The export reproduces the text unchanged” is on, the export structures without AI. This prompt only applies once that option is off.

editor.cleanupRoleDialogue: The AI-smoothed version of the whole transcript — the basis for the translation. With this layout the PDF uses the segments including the speakers.

settings.reasoningHint: Cleanup, translation and PDF structuring are transformations with an explicit instruction — thinking buys nothing there but costs time and the token budget the answer itself needs. If the endpoint does not support the field, Verba stops sending it.
editor.detectSpeakersConfirm: The speakers are recognised again. Existing speaker names are replaced by “Speaker 1”, “Speaker 2” …, and a segment in which the speaker changes is split.
editor.detectSpeakersNoSegments: This recording has not been transcribed yet.
editor.renameSpeakerConfirm: {count} more segments are “{from}”. Rename them to “{to}” as well?
types.diarizeHint: After the transcription it is worked out who speaks when: every segment gets its speaker (“Speaker 1”, “Speaker 2” …), and a segment in which the speaker changes is split at that moment — because Whisper cuts at pauses, not at people, so a segment otherwise holds two voices. That is what a type needs that is a conversation (interview, minutes, roleplay). For a single voice — song, poem, speech, dictation — the option is better left off, where every “second speaker” would be an error. The names are placeholders and can be replaced everywhere with one click in the editor.
speakers.title: Speaker recognition
speakers.intro: Works out who speaks when and splits segments that hold a speaker change.
speakers.typeHint: Two small models compute on the processor, without an account and without an internet connection once downloaded: one finds the stretches of speech, the other recognises the voices again. Whether the recognition runs is not decided on this page but by the transcript type — that is where the switch “Recognise speakers automatically” is. In the editor the recognition can be started by hand for a single recording at any time.
speakers.modelHint: Decides how reliably two voices are told apart. Larger means more accurate and slower; the language of the recording does not matter. The default model is enough for a conversation between clearly different voices, the large ones help with similar voices, many speakers or poor recording quality.
speakers.thresholdHint: How different two voices have to sound to count as two people. The number of speakers is always worked out automatically; this setting is the only knob over it. Lower splits more eagerly and invents speakers, higher merges more readily and throws two people together. 0.5 is the default.
speakers.dirHint: Where the two model files live. A model already lying there is used from there instead of downloaded again — handy when the files come from another machine. Empty means the default directory.
speakers.libraryMissing: The component is not installed yet ({packages}) — install it here, then download the models.
speakers.modelsMissing: Models are still missing — please download them below.
